text:
anita: quick blocking doc issue in PR #4567 — multipart curl example in the Files API page hardcodes a boundary that doesn't match the body. users will copy+pasta and hit 400s.

rachel: saw that in review. i tried the curl snippet and the server rejects it with "malformed multipart".

kevin: can you paste the exact snippets? i can patch it.

anita: sure. current curl block in docs:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryXYZ" \
  --data-binary $'------WebKitFormBoundaryABC
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="test.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

hello
------WebKitFormBoundaryABC--'
```
and the ruby Faraday example on the same page uses the library multipart helper (no explicit boundary). that mismatch is the root cause.

matt: yep header says XYZ but body uses ABC. also --data-binary with a hand-rolled multipart body is brittle. recommendation: switch curl to -F so curl sets the boundary and the example matches the ruby behavior.

rachel: agree. simpler to show `-F "file=@test.txt"` and drop the Content-Type header. add a note: "use -F so curl picks the boundary automatically".

kevin: i'll open a small PR to replace the manual body with `-F` and add a short 201 response example. do we want to also add an explicit comment in the ruby block stating the client sets the boundary?

anita: yes — keep Faraday as-is but add `# Faraday/HTTP client sets the multipart boundary automatically` above the block. don't set Content-Type manually in either example.

kevin: i'll also run the docs lints and link-checker in the branch.

docs-bot: suggested changelog entry: "docs: fix multipart examples (curl -> -F, note for Faraday) to avoid mismatched boundary". queued docs tests. :robot_face:

matt: one more nit — add the minimal 201 response body example we return on successful upload (json with file_id and url). makes it explicit for consumers.

kevin: noted. patch will: replace curl snippet, remove Content-Type header, add ruby comment, add 201 response block, add changelog entry, run tests. pushing in ~8m.

rachel: ping @anita for quick review after you push. want this in before the docs deploy tomorrow.

anita: happy to review. thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
